artifact.rationale: Translations are built from inputs.destination_profile (bucket bravo-demo-attachments, app principal obc-chat-bravo-demo-attachments-…, OpenBao prefix envs/target-onprem/, ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao, namespace chat, SA chat-bravo-demo, Secret bravo-demo-db/password) and from inventory findings inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8, inv:9de663601b600ca9 and inv:c6b9dab5de3d8a70 (Secrets Manager DB secret), and inv:4b2a570efa066af8 and inv:baa6de5a5e72c850 (S3 client/endpoint swap). The evidence is incomplete, so risk is high: inventory_describe returned analysis status 'unconfigured', controls_describe returned gate_unreachable, and the repo snapshot holds only EXAMPLE placeholder values (chart/ci/eks-values.yaml), not the real source IAM role, bucket policy or secret ARN. Because of that, the source ids (attachments-bucket, db-app-secret, chat-app-pod-identity) are descriptive labels, not verified source resource ids. The bucket policy is least privilege for the app principal only: Get/Put/Delete on objects and List on the bucket. It has no anonymous grant, which addresses the OBJ-01 regression (gate:55d795c3-9b37-41fb-93eb-14f031089c7e:obj-01). Other credentials are denied implicitly, which addresses OBJ-05 (gate:55d795c3-9b37-41fb-93eb-14f031089c7e:obj-05). Plain HTTP is refused by a Deny that uses BoolIfExists aws:SecureTransport=false, following the RGW engine fact. The Deny statement's principal '*' and s3:* appear only in that Deny and grant nothing. The rgw target name is chat-bravo-demo-attachments because the lint reserves names starting with 'bravo-'. The policy Resource is still only the profile bucket. Whether the plain-HTTP Deny produces a refusal or a 400 under SSE-KMS (OBJ-06 UNKNOWN risk) must be confirmed by the platform's bucket-test Job. No verdict is asserted.

exception_justifications.justification: No new translation targets encryption at rest. The destination bucket already has SSE-KMS default encryption (kms_key rgw-target-onprem) according to the destination profile, and the OpenBao KV v2 storage keeps its existing platform encryption. Confirmation is left to the gate.

No source audit configuration (CloudTrail or S3 access logging) was available: the inventory analysis is unconfigured and the gate was unreachable. Audit mapping cannot be translated without that evidence, so it needs a human decision.
The proposed artifacts include no network policy, and the source network controls were not provided. Only transport security is covered, through DenyInsecureTransport (ENC-02).
Backup and replication settings for the source bucket and secret were not in the evidence. DR mapping is deferred to a human or the gate.

artifact.audit_summary: Proposal (attempt 1) contains four translations. (1) RGW bucket policy for bravo-demo-attachments. Only the OBC app user gets object Get/Put/Delete and ListBucket. There is no anonymous or other-principal grant, which targets the OBJ-01 and OBJ-05 regressions. Plain HTTP is denied with BoolIfExists aws:SecureTransport=false. (2) OpenBao policy app-target-onprem-chat-db: read only on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db. (3) ExternalSecret chat-bravo-demo-db in namespace chat, using ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao. It maps property app_writer to Secret bravo-demo-db key 'password'. (4) Namespaced Role and RoleBinding chat-bravo-demo-secret-reader: get only on Secret bravo-demo-db, for SA chat-bravo-demo. None of these include wildcard grants, cluster-scoped roles or secret list/watch. Policy lint passed. Risk is HIGH: the source IAM, bucket policy and secret documents were not available (inventory analysis unconfigured, gate unreachable, repo values are EXAMPLE placeholders), and the source ids are descriptive labels. The approver should check against the real source policies. Exceptions are drafted for ENC-01, AUD-01, NET-01 and DR-01. The plain-HTTP outcome under SSE-KMS (OBJ-06) must be confirmed by the bucket-test Job.

artifact.rationale: Removed the direct AWS Secrets Manager dependency (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8 boto3 client at secrets.py:41, inv:9de663601b600ca9 get_secret_value at secrets.py:48) and the DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE selection branch. The DB password is now read only from the mounted file at DB_PASSWORD_FILE (landing zone: ESO syncs OpenBao -> K8s Secret bravo-demo-db, mounted at /var/run/bravo/db/password). config.load() no longer requires or reads DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE, DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_ID/KEY/REGION/ENDPOINT_URL or AWS_REGION, so the app starts with only DB_DSN + DB_PASSWORD_FILE as the destination provides. DbSettings keeps password_source (constant "env-file") so existing log fields (app.py startup log, secrets.py load log) are unchanged; removed secret_id/secret_key/secrets_region/secrets_endpoint_url fields (no other references in app code: app.py, db.py, __main__.py checked). DSN password-guard, attachments/S3 config (already generic S3_ENDPOINT_URL/S3_REGION, inv:baa6de5a5e72c850, inv:4b2a570efa066af8 need no code change), write-block switch and logging untouched. No dependency, test, CI or deploy files changed. Note: the DSN-password guard line in config.py was redacted in tool output; make_diff confirms it is byte-identical to /src (no hunk touches it). Its error message still mentions DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE; left unchanged deliberately to avoid editing a line not visible. compile check passed. Addresses gate regressions gate:55d795c3-9b37-41fb-93eb-14f031089c7e:obj-01 / obj-05 to the extent they stem from startup on destination without cloud secret API.
